source: Drafted from several reference templates including: AICPA_TOWN_HALL_NEWSLETTER_TEMPLATE.html, AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER.html, CPACOM_GENERAL_TEMPLATE.html, CPA_PARTNER_(DOUBLE).html, CPA_PARTNER_(SINGLE).html, DOTCPA_GENERAL_TEMPLATE.html

fonts.note: Present verbatim in the <style> block of all 6 templates.

layout.gmailFontResizeMarkup: - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
layout.note: Confirmed present at the very end of <body> in 5 of 6 templates. DOTCPA_GENERAL_TEMPLATE has it too, just without preceding section markers — see sectionMarkers.knownGaps.

colors.note: Navy (#0f206c) appears as a real brand color in CPACOM_GENERAL_TEMPLATE's footer bar and as the section-header color in AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER ('What's new:' / 'Why it matters:' headers) — it's a legitimate brand accent, not a one-off. Green (#48a23f) is used for partner/co-branded CTAs. AI_IN_FOCUS also uses a one-off cyan (#41b6e6) for its bracket-style 'Read more' buttons — that's template-specific to that newsletter's pre-built button graphic, not part of the general palette; don't reuse it elsewhere.

archetypeOverrides.aiInFocusArticleBody: Article body paragraphs in AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER use font-weight:400, not the usual 300 — this is intentional to this newsletter's denser, punchier tone. Don't 'correct' it to 300 when generating for this archetype.

buttonSystem.description: Marketer-facing Button:/Link:/Color:/Style: syntax in the Instructions column, resolved server-side into brand-consistent button HTML. This is NOT literally present in the raw template files — it's the agent's own generation convention, established and implemented in server.js.

syntax.example:
Button: Register Now
Link: https://cpa.com/register
Color: green
Style: outline

fields.Color: optional — named color or raw hex; defaults to purple

colorMap.note: Raw hex codes are also accepted if given directly.

styles.solid: filled background in the resolved color, white text
styles.outline: white background, colored text and border matching the resolved color

buttonSystem.markup: {text}
buttonSystem.specialCase: AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER's bracket-style 'Read more →' buttons (left/right PNG brackets + colored middle cell) are pre-built INTO that template and are NOT generated by this button system. Treat them like the footer: protected structure. Only href/text may be swapped, and only when explicitly instructed.

textPlaceholders.BODY_CONTENT_HERE: replaced with email body copy written from the ticket description
textPlaceholders.BUTTON_TEXT: replaced with a relevant CTA based on ticket context (legacy single-button templates only — prefer the Button:/Link: syntax for new content)
textPlaceholders.JOB_NUMBER_HERE: replaced with the job number, or the line is removed if blank
textPlaceholders.JOB_NUMBER: replaced with the job number, or the line is removed if blank

mergeTags.note: Any {{...}} or {{{...}}} token is a Pardot merge tag — left exactly as-is, never modified.

sectionMarkers.convention: HTML comment markers delimit protected/structural regions: <!-- START X --> ... <!-- END X -->

observedMarkers.PREHEADER: present in CPA_PARTNER_(DOUBLE) and CPA_PARTNER_(SINGLE) only
observedMarkers.HEADER: present in CPA_PARTNER_(DOUBLE) and CPA_PARTNER_(SINGLE) only
observedMarkers.FOOTER: present in 5 of 6 templates (all except DOTCPA_GENERAL_TEMPLATE)
observedMarkers.MAIN CONTENT: present in AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER only, wraps all article blocks
observedMarkers.ARTICLE: present in AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER, marks the start of each of the 4 article blocks — inconsistently, see knownGaps

knownGaps: DOTCPA_GENERAL_TEMPLATE has NO section markers at all (no START/END FOOTER, no PREHEADER/HEADER). Its footer still exists structurally (black bar + address block), just unmarked. Footer-protection logic needs a fallback for this template — e.g. matching on the 'Black Footer Bar : BEGIN/END' comments, which ARE present in all 6 templates, or wrapping the region by position (everything after the last content table) rather than relying solely on START/END FOOTER.

AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER's article markers are inconsistent: the very first article is preceded by '<!-- ARTICLE MODULE START -->' while each of the 4 articles individually opens with '<!-- START ARTICLE -->' — but there is no matching '<!-- END ARTICLE -->' anywhere. Don't rely on an end-marker for per-article boundaries; the next '<!-- START ARTICLE -->' (or '<!-- END MAIN CONTENT -->' for the last one) is the actual boundary.
CPACOM_GENERAL_TEMPLATE and AICPA_TOWN_HALL_NEWSLETTER_TEMPLATE have FOOTER markers but no PREHEADER/HEADER markers, even though both have a preheader row and header image region structurally.

Recommendation going forward: new templates added to the library should follow the CPA_PARTNER_(SINGLE)/CPA_PARTNER_(DOUBLE) convention (PREHEADER + HEADER + FOOTER all marked) since it's the most complete pattern observed. Worth a light pass to backfill missing markers on the other 4 templates when there's a natural touchpoint (e.g. next time one is revised for a new campaign).

blackFooterBar.marker: <!-- Black Footer Bar : BEGIN --> ... <!-- Black Footer Bar : END -->
blackFooterBar.note: Present in ALL 6 templates without exception, including DOTCPA_GENERAL_TEMPLATE. More reliable as a footer-detection fallback than START/END FOOTER, which DOTCPA_GENERAL_TEMPLATE lacks.

footer.rule: DO NOT MODIFY. Copy verbatim from the matching reference template.
contents: Manage preferences / Unsubscribe / Privacy policy / Contact us / Resubscribe links with exact merge-field tokens (e.g. {{{EmailPreferenceCenter_488}}})
Company address: CPA.com, 1345 Avenue of the Americas, 27th Floor, New York, NY (10105 or 10019 depending on template — do not standardize, copy verbatim per template)
Job number placeholder ({{JobNumber}}, JOB_NUMBER_HERE, or JOB_NUMBER depending on template)
footer.note: Few-shot examples in retrieval prompts may have footers stripped for brevity — the server reattaches the real footer verbatim after generation, so the model never needs to reproduce footer content from an example.

structure: pre-header bold purple link/CTA at the very top
repeating content blocks (image + bold title + description, stacked)

variants.aicpaTownHall: Repeating blocks use a 320x181px image, bold title, short description — each block links out (often to YouTube timestamps in the observed template).
variants.aiInFocus: Denser, magazine-style layout: numbered article modules with a distinct 'What's new:' / 'Why it matters:' two-part structure per article, navy (#0f206c) bold 22px section headers, font-weight 400 body copy (see typeRules.archetypeOverrides), and pre-built bracket-style 'Read more →' buttons in cyan (#41b6e6) — protected structure, see buttonSystem.specialCase.

structure: leanest skeleton, default fallback when nothing else fits

variants.cpacomGeneral: CPA.com brand — footer bar uses navy (#0f206c) instead of the pure black used elsewhere.
variants.dotcpaGeneral: Domains.CPA sub-brand — same general skeleton, branded 'Domains.CPA' wordmark in the footer bar instead of 'CPA.com/', and (see sectionMarkers.knownGaps) lacks section marker comments entirely.

structure: fully marked PREHEADER + HEADER + FOOTER sections (most complete marker convention of the 6 templates)
partner logo lockup in the header, alongside CPA.com's own
'{{Partner}}' merge token used in footer wordmark link (e.g. 'CPA.com/{{Partner}}')
body content otherwise follows the General archetype's structure

variants.double: Two partner logos — used for co-branded content involving two external partners in one send.

partnerCoBranded.note: Not called out as a 4th top-level archetype in the original 3-archetype list (Newsletter/General), but structurally distinct enough (partner logo handling, {{Partner}} token, black bgcolor footer bar) to warrant its own tag/archetype value in the manifest rather than being folded into 'general'.

toneRules: Never invent a destination URL, discount code, or stat.
Confirm personalization token usage ({{Recipient.FirstName}}) if ambiguous rather than assuming.
Match the tone notes of the retrieved few-shot template's use case.

AI_IN_FOCUS_NEWSLETTER's article copy runs denser and more analytical (see the 'grounded machine' example article) than the punchier, shorter-paragraph style of AICPA_TOWN_HALL_NEWSLETTER_TEMPLATE's blocks — match density to archetype variant, not just archetype.
